correctness.rationale: The tensor-algebra coefficient argument proves injectivity of the bracket by every nonzero degree-one vector on the degree-two free Lie part in every characteristic. The lower-central filtration argument identifies all possible pair-generated types; disjoint degree-one rank strata give exact ordered counts. Uniform numbers of generating ordered pairs in the abelian, Heisenberg and free class-three types give exact distinct-subalgebra counts. Direct exhaustion over fields of orders two and three confirms both spectra for two generators, with separate samples for ranks three and four. The finite tests supplement, rather than replace, the general proof.

value.rationale: Counts of subalgebras generated by two elements are a natural refinement of subgroup/subalgebra growth and random-generation invariants. The result classifies both object types and all counting fibers for unbounded nilpotency rank and every finite field, with a sharp missing dimension four, a Heisenberg/free rank transition, and a full distinct-subalgebra formula rather than a fixed-size computation. These exact invariants cannot be read off merely from the number of elements or automorphism-group order. The centralizer decomposition gives an independent structural interpretation.
